title: Detecting a quasi-isomorphism of perfect complexes on a neighbourhood
statement: For a chain map between strictly perfect complexes on an affine open, if its induced map on the stalk complex at a point is a quasi-isomorphism, then it is a quasi-isomorphism after restricting to some affine open containing the point and contained in the original open [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-perfect-complex] [def-pc-module-stalk-functor].

proof.text: Taking stalks carries each finite-free retraction to a projective stalk module, so the stalk complexes are K-projective by CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective. Mathlib's quasi-isomorphism criterion supplies a homotopy equivalence whose forward map is the given stalk map of f.

Lift the inverse homotopy equivalence by the existing affine perfect open stalk chain-map lifting theorem. Use the canonical openModuleStalkRestrictionComparison and its naturality to transport both inverse homotopies to the restriction of f composed with the lift and the reverse composite.

Apply the inverse-homotopies spreading theorem to obtain an affine W and a chain map giving both inverse homotopies for the exact restriction of f. Assemble HomotopyEquiv and apply HomotopyEquiv.quasiIso_hom. The source proof ignores the old hU binder, so the original node statement is recovered by specialization.

theorem exists_affine_restriction_quasiIso_of_perfect_stalk_quasiIso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (P Q : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hP : IsStrictlyPerfect X U P) (hQ : IsStrictlyPerfect X U Q) (f : P ⟶ Q)
    (hf : QuasiIso (((openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).map f)) :
    ∃ (W : X.Opens) (_hxW : x ∈ W) (_hW : IsAffineOpen W) (hWU : W ≤ U),
      QuasiIso (((SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)
        (homOfLE hWU : W ⟶ U)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f)
